monogr.title: Output Specification -Return type and format of the output
5 Core Behaviour -Essential functional steps the code must perform, usually mapped to a problem domain
Constraints & Robustness Sets performance and correctness boundaries for safe
Complexity Targets -Desired time and space complexity
Environment Constraints -Platform, language

biblStruct.note: or hardware requirements (e.g., "no recursion due to stack limit"

monogr.title: Edge Case Handling -Explicit mention of inputs like empty arrays, max values, or special formats
Error Handling -Required exception behavior, validation, or fallback logic
Data Invariants -Conditions

biblStruct.note: that must hold true before/after execution (e.g., "list remains sorted"

monogr.title: Solution Structure & Design Guidance Guides how the solution should be implemented or structured
Specifying Algorithmic Strategy -Recommends a general technique
Specifying Data Structure -Recommends a structure

biblStruct.note: e.g., array, set, tree, heap) to enable efficient access

monogr.title: Forbidden Techniques -Prohibits certain APIs, heuristics
Implementation Sketch or Step Breakdown -Provides a sequence of logical steps or pseudocode
Common Implementation Patterns -Highlights structural motifs (e.g., prefix sum, twopointer
Role or Persona Framing -Adopts a tone or style based on audience
4 Verification & Integration Specifies how correctness is tested and how the code fits into a larger system
1 Sample I/O Pairs -Concrete examples showing expected outputs for given inputs
Unit Tests or Oracle Checks -Lists or refers to test cases that must pass
3 Integration Context -Describes where/how the code will be called or embedded
Dependencies -External libraries, packages
